'''George Hermann Büchi''' (August 1, 1921 – August 28, 1998) was a Swiss [[organic chemist]] and professor at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]]. "Paternò's reaction", known since the early twentieth century,<ref>{{Cite journal |first1= E. |last1= Paterno |first2= G. |last2= Chieffi |journal= [[Gazzetta Chimica Italiana]] |volume = 39 |issue = 2 |pages = 341–361 |year = 1909 | title = Synthesis in organic chemistry using light. Note II. Compounds of unsaturated hydrocarbons with aldehydes and ketones.}}</ref> was renamed to the "[[Paternò–Büchi reaction]]" based on enhancements made to it by Büchi's research group.<ref>{{Cite journal | title =  Light-catalyzed Organic Reactions. I. The Reaction of Carbonyl Compounds with 2-Methyl-2-butene in the Presence of Ultraviolet Light|author1=G. Büchi |author2=Charles G. Inman |author3=E. S. Lipinsky | journal =  [[Journal of the American Chemical Society]]| volume = 76 | issue = 17| pages = 4327–4331 | year = 1954| doi = 10.1021/ja01646a024   }}</ref>

Büchi died at the age of 77 of heart failure while hiking with his wife in Switzerland.<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://www.nap.edu/read/10169/chapter/4#15|doi = 10.17226/10169|title = Biographical Memoirs|year = 2001|isbn = 978-0-309-07572-5}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/1998/09/08/us/george-h-buchi-organic-chemist-dies-at-77.html|title=George H. Buchi, Organic Chemist, Dies at 77|newspaper=The New York Times|date=8 September 1998|last1=Saxon|first1=Wolfgang}}</ref>
